rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle with old photos they only vaguely remember, across several kinds. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Among memories like people, trips, and events, 13 of 48 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]] Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the same — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]] For receipts, documents, or notes, 8 of 21 stories say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] One person wrote “I need old screenshot picc.” [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of what went wrong for each kind?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details do people actually remember about a photo (what, when, who, where, event, etc.) versus what they forgot or were wrong about?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell which details people remember, because two AI readers agreed on that too rarely to rely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]][[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

People most often remembered what was in the photo: 47 of 115 stories (41%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Some remembered when it was taken: 24 of 115 stories (21%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Fewer remembered who was in it: 14 of 115 stories (12%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
One person said they had to scroll past “many bill hader pictures” to reach a year they wanted. [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a short list of the least-remembered details too?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What kinds of details about the target photo did people report forgetting when trying to find it?
rows.text:
People often forgot key details about the photo itself. [[analysis_coverage|2.4]] Many stories only said a little about what they remembered, so clues were thin. [[analysis_coverage|2.1]] Only 48 of 331 stories say anything about whether anything in the image could be searched for, so people often lacked object or text details. [[analysis_coverage|0.3]] One person even said they “couldn’t think how I’d figure out where” to look for a medlar photo. [[story|112f493208a69edd002fcc3b5194ae1643a18c55:0]] Only 3 of 115 stories say anything about whether date, place and faces were recorded correctly. [[analysis_coverage|0.2]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a split by stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple word for what they remember, like bicycle, a poster’s text, or an object or action. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]][[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]]
In 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Some people skip dates and rely on visual clues in words, such as “bicycle” or text in the scene. [[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]][[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]]
One person tried “vomit” and got nothing: “no result for vomit”. [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a brief summary of the words people tried most?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
Often, yes — many stories say the search did not understand the words people typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
This happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
Some people did find photos with search, showing it can work. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]  
One person said “I can’t find my photos wearing green clothes kit of football.” [[story|912c6cc3068a194559168f5b66e2dbc5bc867dc8:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick view of other first problems people ran into?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo, so they cannot answer what Google Photos’ annual revenue is.  
They cannot answer this because they are not business records or usage data.  
A financial report or audited company filings would be needed to answer.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories cannot answer this, because they are public posts about trying to find a photo, not usage records, so they cannot show monthly active users of Ask Photos. These posts also cannot show any rate of success or failure. Data that could answer this would be official usage metrics, such as monthly active users from product analytics or company reports.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: These are public posts about trying to find a photo, so they cannot tell us any rate of success or failure. They also cannot give a count of users or searches. A proper answer would need usage data that tracks all vague-memory searches and their outcomes.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.text:
These stories cannot say whether Android users struggle more than iPhone users, because the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What they do show is where searches first went wrong in stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
In 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
In 20 of 115 stories (17%), the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
One person said it “took me forever to find it” [[story|4217b5d02ba957a72904fa796a4bd54327cf19d2:0]]. 

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of other ways people got stuck?*

[[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about the system discarded the photo because one detail was wrong — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
Few public posts say anything about one wrong detail hiding the photo, so this is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]

A wrong year can act like a hard filter, but posts that name this are rare. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]] In 1 of 115 stories (1%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the post says adding more words made the photo disappear. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]] In 2 of 115 stories (2%), a small mistake in a detail did not matter. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=soft_ok@photo_class:_all]] One person wrote “it says no results” when they added words. [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.restated: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell how many attempts people make before they give up, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on this. [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]][[analysis_reliability|q:8.1]]

Some do stop after one try: 21 of 115 stories (18%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered say one try. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Some keep at it for a few tries over some minutes: 6 of 115 stories (5%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
A few say an hour or more: 3 of 115 stories (3%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One person wrote “No matter how many times I look back at the photos, I can't find a shot” [[story|3f6c7b626f52b658b0c519881ff8cb6967208570:0]].

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.text:
Most often, it fails because the search does not understand what people type, or it shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
This happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
Next, the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else — in 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
withheld: unverifiable quote: today just did ‘Kids’ and after scrolling enough it was right there.
rows.draft:
Fix search understanding first. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] It is the one problem with enough stories to rank, with 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo saying search did not understand or match what they typed. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Apply AI to better read simple cues, link them to people, places, and time, and strengthen concept and entity indexing. [[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:intelligence_needed]] One post shows the kind of thin cue people try: “today just did ‘Kids’ and after scrolling enough it was right there.” [[story|b2358d9efca162742579284a99c00a353586c178:0]][[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:chain:evidence]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see examples of cues that search missed?*
rows.text:
- The problem — search did not understand or match what they typed — comes up in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 30 people. It is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]]
- The problem — the photo was gone before anyone searched — deleted, never backed up, elsewhere — comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 20 people. Better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]]
- The problem — they never searched — scrolled the timeline or didn't know search could help — comes up in 9 of 115 stories (8%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 9 people. Too few stories to rank it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage3]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Most often, the search shows the wrong photos or does not understand what they typed when they look for a pet photo.
